title: Honesty, Lies & Excuses
description: From your course: confessions, lies and cons, cheating in exams, excuses at work and getting caught out.

items.definition: telling people about something bad or embarrassing that you did
items.example: OK, [confession] time: I still haven't read the book for our book club.
items.exampleRu: Ладно, каюсь: я так и не прочитал книгу для нашего книжного клуба.
items.pattern: make a confession / have a confession to make
items.trap: «Признание» meaning recognition of your work is 'recognition', not 'confession'; and you 'make' a confession, not 'do' one.

items.definition: not considered polite or acceptable in a particular group or place
items.example: Where I work, it's [not the done thing] to talk about your salary.
items.exampleRu: У нас на работе не принято обсуждать свою зарплату.
items.pattern: it's (not) the done thing to do sth
items.trap: Mainly British. Don't calque «не принято» as 'it's not accepted to…'; say 'it's not the done thing to…' or 'people don't usually…'.

items.definition: feeling bad and guilty because of something wrong you did
items.example: Looking back, I'm quite [ashamed of] how rude I was to that waiter.
items.exampleRu: Теперь мне довольно стыдно за то, как грубо я разговаривал с тем официантом.
items.pattern: be ashamed of sth / of doing sth
items.trap: 'Ashamed' is about doing something wrong; for silly, awkward moments use 'embarrassed'.

items.definition: to trick someone, usually to get their money
items.example: The taxi driver at the airport [conned us] out of thirty euros.
items.exampleRu: Таксист в аэропорту развёл нас на тридцать евро.
items.pattern: con sb out of sth / con sb into doing sth
items.trap: Informal. «Развести на деньги» is 'con sb out of money', never 'divorce'; and 'cheat on sb' means being unfaithful.

items.definition: to make someone believe something that is not true
items.example: Don't be [deceived] by the photos: the hotel is much smaller in real life.
items.exampleRu: Не ведись на фотографии: в реальности отель намного меньше.
items.pattern: deceive sb / be deceived by sth
items.trap: 'Deceive' is quite strong and formal; in everyday speech people say 'lie to sb' or 'be fooled by sth'.

items.definition: to make someone believe something wrong, by what you say or don't say
items.example: Apologies if I [misled] you about the deadline: it's actually Friday, not Thursday.
items.exampleRu: Прошу прощения, если ввёл вас в заблуждение насчёт дедлайна: на самом деле он в пятницу, а не в четверг.
items.pattern: mislead sb (about sth) / mislead sb into doing sth
items.trap: The past form is 'misled', not 'misleaded'; don't confuse it with 'mislaid' (= lost).

items.definition: not suitable or not polite for a particular situation
items.example: Is it [inappropriate] to message my boss on WhatsApp at the weekend?
items.exampleRu: Писать начальнику в WhatsApp на выходных — это неуместно?
items.pattern: it's inappropriate to do sth / inappropriate for sb/sth
items.trap: The prefix is 'in-', not 'un-'; and «неадекватный» is not 'inadequate' (= not good enough).

items.definition: to be thought of as bad or wrong by most people
items.example: Using your phone at the dinner table is [frowned on] in my family.
items.exampleRu: У нас в семье не одобряют, когда сидят в телефоне за ужином.
items.pattern: sth is frowned on/upon
items.trap: 'Frowned upon' means the same and is a little more formal; 'frown at sb' just means looking at sb angrily.

items.definition: so bad that it shocks people and should not be allowed
items.example: Our landlord took four months to fix the heating, which is [shockingly unacceptable].
items.exampleRu: Наш арендодатель четыре месяца чинил отопление — это просто возмутительно.
items.pattern: sth is shockingly unacceptable
items.trap: It's 'unacceptable', never 'inacceptable'; and the adverb 'shockingly', not the adjective 'shocking', goes before an adjective.

items.definition: to find the answers in a book or online instead of working them out yourself
items.example: At the pub quiz, my mate kept trying to [look up the answers] on his phone.
items.exampleRu: На квизе в пабе мой приятель всё пытался подсмотреть ответы в телефоне.
items.pattern: look up sth / look sth up / look it up
items.trap: With a pronoun the particle goes last: 'look it up', not 'look up it'.

items.definition: to have no time left before you finish something
items.example: In the exam I [ran out of time] and left two questions blank.
items.exampleRu: На экзамене мне не хватило времени, и два вопроса я так и оставил без ответа.
items.pattern: run out of sth
items.trap: Don't say 'my time finished' or 'I didn't manage'; 'I ran out of time' is the natural way to say «не успел».

items.definition: to study again what you have learnt so you are ready for an exam
items.example: No nights out for me this week: I'm [revising for an exam] on Monday.
items.exampleRu: На этой неделе никаких тусовок: готовлюсь к экзамену в понедельник.
items.pattern: revise (sth) for an exam
items.trap: British English; Americans say 'review'. «Повторять» here is never 'repeat'.

items.definition: to be good enough to succeed or to reach the standard needed
items.example: Sadly, I didn't [make the grade] for the team lead role this time.
items.exampleRu: К сожалению, на позицию тимлида я в этот раз не прошёл.
items.pattern: make the grade (as sth / for sth)
items.trap: It's not about school marks: it means being good enough. The verb is 'make', not 'do'.

items.definition: without other people seeing or knowing
items.example: My flatmate [secretly] eats my yoghurts and thinks I don't notice.
items.exampleRu: Мой сосед по квартире тайком ест мои йогурты и думает, что я не замечаю.
items.trap: «Тайком от кого-то» is 'without sb knowing', not 'secretly from sb'.

items.definition: to have done so little or so badly that failing is fair
items.example: To be fair, I didn't revise at all, so I [deserved to fail].
items.exampleRu: Если честно, я вообще не готовился, так что провалился заслуженно.
items.pattern: deserve to do sth / deserve sth
items.trap: No preposition after 'deserve': 'deserve a break', not 'deserve for a break'.

items.translation: объявление, реклама (job advert — объявление о вакансии)
items.definition: a notice, picture or short film that tells people about a product, job or service
items.example: Just saw a job [advert] that looks perfect for you — sending you the link!
items.exampleRu: Только что увидел вакансию, которая тебе идеально подходит, — кидаю ссылку!
items.pattern: an advert for sth
items.trap: 'Advert' and 'ad' are British; 'advertisement' is formal. «Реклама» in general is 'advertising' (uncountable); one item is 'an advert'.

items.definition: to make something sound bigger, better or worse than it really is
items.example: Honestly, I'm not [exaggerating]: the queue at passport control was two hours long.
items.exampleRu: Честно, я не преувеличиваю: очередь на паспортном контроле была на два часа.
items.pattern: exaggerate (sth)
items.trap: Spelling: double 'g', single 'r' — exaggerate.

items.definition: telling the truth is always the best choice, even when it is difficult
items.example: I told my boss I'd forgotten about the report — [honesty is the best policy], right?
items.exampleRu: Я признался начальнику, что забыл про отчёт, — честность лучшая политика, правда?
items.trap: Here 'policy' means a way of acting, not 'politics'.
wrong: the honesty is the best policy

items.definition: making you feel silly or uncomfortable in front of other people
items.example: That was so [embarrassing]: I called my new manager by the wrong name.
items.exampleRu: Было так неловко: я назвал нового начальника чужим именем.
items.pattern: it's embarrassing to do sth / I'm embarrassed
items.trap: 'Embarrassing' describes the situation; 'embarrassed' is how you feel: 'I was embarrassed', not 'I was embarrassing'.

items.definition: to want very much to make people think well of you
items.example: It's my first week, so I'm really [keen to impress] my new team.
items.exampleRu: Это моя первая неделя, так что мне очень хочется произвести впечатление на новую команду.
items.pattern: be keen to do sth / be keen on sth
items.trap: 'Keen to + verb' but 'keen on + noun/-ing': keen to impress, keen on football.

items.definition: a worker with a low position and less experience than others
items.example: Being the most [junior staff member] in the office isn't always easy.
items.exampleRu: Быть самым младшим сотрудником в офисе не всегда легко.
items.trap: 'Junior' is about rank, not age; and 'staff' (персонал) is not 'stuff' (вещи).

items.definition: to say or let people think that you did something good that someone else did
items.example: My manager [took credit for] my idea in front of the whole team.
items.exampleRu: Начальник при всей команде выдал мою идею за свою.
items.pattern: take (the) credit for sth / for doing sth
items.trap: No 'a': 'a credit' is money from a bank. Say 'take (the) credit for sth'.

items.definition: to have someone as your manager at work
items.example: Who do you [report to] in your new job?
items.exampleRu: Кому ты подчиняешься на новой работе?
items.pattern: report to sb
items.trap: «Подчиняться начальнику» at work is 'report to sb', not 'obey' or 'be subordinate to'.

items.definition: to see something happen, especially a crime or an accident
items.example: On my way to work this morning, I [witnessed] a car accident.
items.exampleRu: Сегодня утром по дороге на работу я стал свидетелем аварии.
items.pattern: witness sth / be a witness to sth
items.trap: As a verb it needs no preposition: 'I witnessed an accident'; avoid the calque 'I became a witness of…'.

items.definition: a crime when someone takes things from a person in the street, often using force
items.example: There was a [street robbery] right outside my building last night.
items.exampleRu: Вчера вечером прямо у моего дома был уличный грабёж.
items.trap: In everyday British English people often say 'mugging' ('I got mugged'). You rob a person or a place, but you steal a thing.

items.definition: to run or drive after someone or something to catch them
items.example: I [chased] the bus all the way down the street, but it didn't stop.
items.exampleRu: Я бежал за автобусом через всю улицу, но он так и не остановился.
items.pattern: chase sb/sth / chase after sb/sth
items.trap: No 'for': 'chase the bus' or 'chase after the bus'. At work, 'chase sb up' means reminding them to do something.

items.definition: a person who steals things
items.example: Hold on to your bag on the metro: [thieves] often target tourists there.
items.exampleRu: В метро держи сумку крепче: воры там часто охотятся на туристов.
items.trap: Plural is 'thieves', not 'thiefs'. A thief steals secretly; a robber uses force or threats.

items.definition: to change the facts so the story is not completely true
items.example: I didn't lie — I just [altered the facts] a little!
items.exampleRu: Я не врал — я просто слегка подправил факты!
items.trap: «Исказить факты» is 'alter', 'twist' or 'distort' the facts; 'alter' (change) sounds the same as 'altar' (in a church).

items.definition: to say something in an indirect way; a small, indirect piece of information
items.example: My sister keeps [hinting] that she'd love a new phone for her birthday.
items.exampleRu: Сестра всё время намекает, что была бы рада новому телефону на день рождения.
items.pattern: hint that… / hint at sth / drop a hint
items.trap: Say 'hint at sth' or 'hint that…', not 'hint on sth'; and 'drop a hint', not 'make a hint'.

items.definition: to phone work and say you are too ill to come in
items.example: If you're ill, just [call in sick] — don't come in and infect everyone.
items.exampleRu: Если заболел, просто отпросись по болезни — не приходи и не заражай всех.
items.pattern: call in sick (to work)
items.trap: For a longer, official absence say 'be on sick leave'; «взять больничный» is never 'take a hospital'.

items.definition: to be allowed not to go to work on a particular day
items.example: Do you think I could [get the day off] on Friday for my cousin's wedding?
items.exampleRu: Как думаете, можно мне в пятницу взять выходной на свадьбу двоюродного брата?
items.pattern: get/take/have the day off (work)
items.trap: «Выходной» is 'a day off', not 'a free day' or 'a weekend'.

items.definition: a short pause or doubt before you do or say something
items.example: When they offered me the job in Lisbon, I said yes without [hesitation].
items.exampleRu: Когда мне предложили работу в Лиссабоне, я согласился не раздумывая.
items.pattern: without (a moment's) hesitation
items.trap: «Колебание» in science is 'vibration' or 'oscillation'; only doubt is 'hesitation'.

items.definition: to work extra time later because you worked less earlier
items.example: Can I leave early for the dentist and [make up the hours] on Thursday?
items.exampleRu: Можно я уйду пораньше к стоматологу, а часы отработаю в четверг?
items.pattern: make up the hours/time (later)
items.trap: Natives say 'make up the hours', not 'catch up the hours'; 'work out the hours' means calculating them.

items.definition: not wanting to do something, so you do it slowly or not at all
items.example: After last time, I'm a bit [reluctant to lend] him money again.
items.exampleRu: После прошлого раза мне как-то не хочется снова давать ему в долг.
items.pattern: be reluctant to do sth
items.trap: Use 'to + verb', not 'of' or '-ing': 'reluctant to lend', not 'reluctant of lending'.

items.translation: смотреть в глаза, установить зрительный контакт
items.definition: to look directly into someone's eyes while they look at you
items.example: Try to [make eye contact] in interviews, even when you're nervous.
items.exampleRu: На собеседованиях старайся смотреть в глаза, даже если нервничаешь.
items.pattern: make eye contact (with sb)
items.trap: The verb is 'make', not 'do' or 'set'; and it's 'eye contact', not 'eyes contact'.

items.definition: something bad that happens to you because you did something wrong
items.example: As a [punishment] for being late, I had to buy coffee for everyone.
items.exampleRu: В наказание за опоздание мне пришлось покупать кофе на всех.
items.pattern: punishment for sth / for doing sth
items.trap: Use 'for', not 'of': 'punishment for being late'.

items.definition: to be shown to be lying or not prepared, often by a question or a surprise
items.example: Never lie about seeing a film — you'll get [caught out] in five minutes.
items.exampleRu: Никогда не ври, что смотрел фильм, — спалишься через пять минут.
collocations: be caught out by the rain
items.pattern: be/get caught out (by sth)
items.trap: Mainly British. It also means being unprepared: 'We got caught out by the rain.'

items.definition: to fall to the ground when you are standing or walking
items.example: I [fell over] on the ice outside my flat and hurt my knee.
items.exampleRu: Я упал на льду возле дома и ушиб колено.
items.pattern: fall over / fall over sth (= trip on it)
items.trap: «Споткнуться» is 'trip (over sth)': you can trip without falling over. The past is 'fell', not 'felt'.

items.definition: to want to do something, often something you know you shouldn't
items.example: I was so [tempted to order] pizza, but I made a salad instead.
items.exampleRu: Мне ужасно хотелось заказать пиццу, но я сделал себе салат.
items.pattern: be tempted to do sth / be tempted by sth
items.trap: 'I was tempted' is how you feel; 'it was tempting' describes the thing.

items.definition: so attractive that you can't stop yourself wanting it
items.example: The smell from the bakery near my office is [impossible to resist].
items.exampleRu: Перед запахом из пекарни возле моего офиса просто невозможно устоять.
items.pattern: sth is impossible to resist
items.trap: 'Resist' takes no preposition: 'resist the cake', not 'resist to the cake' or 'resist against it'.
